summary: Secure Wipe & Reset (factory reset) returns the appliance to a clean state. New infra/db/bootstrap Reset(ctx, opts) drops the whole database (postgres: best-effort terminate sessions then DROP DATABASE ... WITH (FORCE) — which itself evicts any remaining connections on PG13+ — with a plain-DROP fallback for older servers; mariadb: DROP DATABASE; sqlite: delete the db + wal/shm/journal) then re-runs Ensure() to recreate the schema and re-seed stock data — gated by bootstrap.allowReset (default false). A reusable apphost.Restarter primitive (Dependencies.Restarter + relaunchSelf, a detached copy of the executable that then exits) relaunches the process cleanly on both bare metal (child takes over) and docker/systemd (clean exit -> supervisor relaunch); it is also intended for a future self-update. services.SystemResetService orchestrates: shred all media (snapshot dir, training dir, fileStorage uploads, per-camera recording paths, with guards so it can never nuke the working directory) -> bootstrap.Reset -> restart, reporting in-memory ResetProgress. As a deliberate security measure the orchestrator is best-effort and ALWAYS drives to a restart: a file that can't be shredded or a database-wipe error is recorded as a non-fatal warning (the restart re-runs bootstrap and can finish an interrupted rebuild) rather than aborting. API (apis/system.go): POST /api/system/reset (admin-write + allowReset), GET /api/system/reset/state, GET /api/system/reset/progress. UI: a Danger Zone in Machine Health (only when reset is allowed) with a 10s auto-proceed countdown modal and a full-screen progress overlay that polls progress then /health and reloads on recovery. Also in this batch: manual 'Purge expired' buttons on the Recording page (POST /api/recording/segments/purge) and Notification settings (POST /api/notifications/purge), and a 1-day minimum recording retention floor in the capacity estimator so the disk balances cameras against retention instead of zeroing either.
compatibility: Disabled by default — the button is hidden unless bootstrap.allowReset=true. The reset is irreversible and intentionally unstoppable: the postgres drop is forced and stage errors become warnings rather than aborts, so it shreds all media and drops the database (recreated empty + re-seeded with the default admin) and always restarts. config.json is NOT touched (runtime settings live in the DB and are reset with it). Docker deployments need a restart policy for the post-reset relaunch; bare-metal uses relaunchSelf.
